findings.issue_text: [High/bug] GroupAdapter.java:273 — getSubGroupsCount() can return null when the cached entry has been invalidated concurrently; callers assigning to primitive long will get an NPE from unboxing, just relocating the original NPE. Better fix is to fall back to the real store (session.groups().getSubGroupsCount(this)) or return 0L while keeping the Long return contract.

[Medium/test_gap] GroupTest.java:137-151 — the reader thread is never joined before assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty()) runs; the thread may append an exception after the assertion executes, so the test can intermittently pass even when the bug reproduces. Capture the thread, join it, then assert.

[Medium/test_gap] GroupTest.java:132-143 — the reader thread is a raw non-daemon Thread with no name and no failure propagation; if managedRealm.admin() hangs or the framework tears down the realm/session, the thread can outlive the test and leak resources/connections. Use an ExecutorService with timeout or a daemon thread plus join with timeout.

[Low/performance] GroupTest.java:138 — the reader loop is a hot busy-wait issuing unthrottled admin REST requests with no sleep/backoff, flooding the server during the delete phase and making the test slow and prone to timeouts. Add a small Thread.sleep between iterations.

[Low/test_gap] GroupTest.java:142 — the catch block only collects exceptions into caughtExceptions without preserving context; on assertion failure the original stack trace is never logged, making CI failures hard to diagnose. Record or print stack traces on failure.

goldens.comment: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.
The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

Use an ExecutorService with timeout or a daemon thread plus join with timeout.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupTest#createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti, the diff introduces `new Thread(() -> { while (!deletedAll.get()) { managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...); } }).start();` without keeping a reference, marking it daemon, naming it, or joining it with a timeout. Because it is a non-daemon thread and the loop body performs a potentially blocking admin call, the thread can outlive the test (e.g., if the call blocks or teardown occurs) and keep the JVM alive / leak resources. Exceptions are only collected and not used to stop the thread or fail early, so failures may not be propagated promptly.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, a background thread runs `while (!deletedAll.get()) { managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(null, 0, Integer.MAX_VALUE, true); }` with no sleep/backoff. This is a tight busy-wait loop issuing unthrottled REST calls, which can overload the server during deletions and make the test slow/flaky (timeouts), matching the finding.

adjudication.rationale: In the new test `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti`, the reader thread catches `Exception e` and only does `caughtExceptions.add(e);` with no logging. The final assertion `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` will fail without showing stack traces (likely only `Exception.toString()`), making CI failures harder to debug. This is a test diagnosability gap, not a product bug.
